archetype: Burst-window bossing thief. Stacks debuffs on the boss, then dumps a short, very high burst from close range. No lifesteal, and the whole damage profile is built around a single-target burst that must land inside the Ring of Restraint window.

linkSkill.name: Thief's Cunning
linkSkill.effect: Passive. Debuffing an enemy grants roughly +18% damage for about 10 seconds, on a ~20 second internal cooldown. Stacks up to three times when three different Explorer Thieves contribute.

legionEffect: Critical Rate, scaling +1% through +5% as more Night Lord legion characters are placed.

vMatrix.systemNote: As of v.271 the V Matrix is point-based and every player receives a fixed set of 6 boost nodes, each enhancing between 1 and 4 individual skills (maplestorywiki, V Matrix). Boost nodes max at level 60 and must reach level 40 to unlock their corresponding HEXA Mastery node. Crafting your own 3-skill 'trios' is no longer part of the system; the Night Lord class doc's version history for 11 July 2026 records that it simplified its V Matrix section 'now that trios are gone'.

priority.why: Top-priority boost node. Quad Star is the main single-target attack and this node gates HEXA Quad Star, the first HEXA mastery core. Grandis's PRIMARY tier is defined as 'Boost Nodes that unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery and are skills that are frequently used', which this node satisfies.
Second boost node. Assassin's Mark is a passive follow-up attack that fires constantly, so its node scales a large share of total output, and it gates HEXA Assassin's Mark (mastery core 2).

One boost node holding both mobbing skills, so there is nothing to rank between them - levelling the node levels both. Showdown is the primary mobbing skill and the source of the party-wide Untouchable effect; Dark Flare is a placed summon that can clear a screen on its own with enough drop and meso gear. The node gates mastery core 3 (HEXA Dark Flare / HEXA Showdown / Darkness Shuriken).

priority.node: Node 4 - Death Star and Sudden Raid
priority.why: The fourth and last node worth levelling, again holding two skills in one node with no ranking between them. Death Star is a 14-second-cooldown bossing skill that matters mostly because it drives Throw Blasting charm consumption; the class doc describes Sudden Raid as only useful when you are out of range of the boss. The node gates mastery core 4 (HEXA Sudden Raid / HEXA Death Star).

priority.node: Node 5 - Triple Throw and Shuriken Challenge
priority.why: Explicitly not built. The class doc marks this grouping Skip; Grandis files it under Other, defined as 'Boost Nodes that do not need to be upgraded or has least priority'. Neither skill unlocks a HEXA mastery.

priority.node: Node 6 - Gust Charm and Shuriken Burst
priority.why: Explicitly not built, same reasoning as node 5.

vMatrix.priorityNote: The array is ordered because both the class doc and Grandis Library number these nodes 1 through 6 in this order. Within nodes 3 and 4 the two skills share a single boost node, so no ordering between them exists or is claimed; "skillsOrdered": false marks that. Do not render those pairs as a ranking.
vMatrix.triosNote: DELETED, not missing. Boost node trios were removed from the game. maplestorywiki's V Matrix page states every player now receives a fixed set of 6 boost nodes rather than crafting 3-skill combinations, and the Night Lord class doc's 11 July 2026 version-history entry says it simplified its V Matrix section 'now that trios are gone'. mastermysty's node guide still publishes Night Lord trios (Trio 1 Showdown / Quad Star / Assassin's Mark, Trio 2 Sudden Raid / Death Star / Dark Flare) but its data is dated 2024-05-14 and predates the change, and its groupings contradict the current six-node layout, which pairs Showdown with Dark Flare and Death Star with Sudden Raid. A previous revision of this file presented those trios as confirmed by the class doc and Grandis Library; neither source contains them.

jobNodeOrder.note: Class doc V-job node priority, highest first. Shadow Walker and Last Resort share one cell in the doc's table and are therefore tied, not ranked; they are nested in an inner array for that reason.

commonNodes.order: Highest to lowest priority per the class doc: level the decent shared skills to 1 (Combat Orders, Sharp Eyes, Speed Infusion, Advanced Blessing); then Erda Nova to level 25 for a 120-second cooldown, or simply max it to 30 if you would rather not manage cooldown desync; Erda Shower and Erda Fountain are low priority because they are already much stronger than Dark Flare and Assassin's Mark, so one-shotting is not the constraint.

vMatrix.notes: Training caveat from the class doc: if Dark Flare is not killing in one or two hits in Grandis maps you cannot lean on the summon and end up running a circular rotation instead. Separately, being heavily overgeared for a map reduces Sol Janus: Dusk procs, so Dark Flare clear speed and Dusk synergy pull against each other. IED CORRECTION: an earlier revision of this file claimed the Quad Star and Assassin's Mark boost nodes are special sources of +20% Ignore Enemy Defense. They are not. Per maplestorywiki's V Matrix page, boost nodes generally grant +20% Ignored Enemy Defense at level 40, and the class doc's own IED section was rewritten in October 2024 to EXCLUDE boost-node IED from gear planning, because much of Night Lord's damage comes from skill (job) nodes, which grant no IED. Do not treat boost-node IED as a Night Lord-specific advantage and do not count it when planning visual IED.

nodeLayout.classCommonCoreNote: NAME RECONCILIATION. This one node appears under two names across the sources and both are now recorded. The class doc's HEXA final-damage table lists it under 'Common Skills' as 'Ultimate Dark Sight'; the v271 tracker spreadsheet tracks the same node, with type 'ClassCommon' and 31 levels, under the name 'Shadow Walker'. Shadow Walker is the underlying 5th job skill shared by Night Lord, Shadower and Blade Master (maplestorywiki), and Ultimate Dark Sight VI is the job-group common HEXA core introduced in KMS ver. 1.2.414 (April 2026) that enhances it - its description, 'your stealth techniques are refined to their limits, allowing you to attack and use skills in Dark Sight without it being cancelled', matches Shadow Walker's effect. GMS availability at v.271: the GMS-facing v271 tracker and the class doc's GMS HEXA table both include the node, but maplestorywiki's Night Lord/Skills page does not yet list it among Shared HEXA Skills and a wiki-wide search for 'Ultimate Dark Sight' returns zero hits, so treat the GMS name as unconfirmed by the wiki. If searching in-game, look for the Shadow Walker enhancement.
nodeLayout.notes: Mastery core slots 3 and 4 each offer a choice; slots 1 and 2 do not. The available-core lists are game facts taken from maplestorywiki. The chosen-core list is judgement: the Night Lord Discord's own v271 tracker levels Dark Flare for slot 3 (over Showdown and Darkness Shuriken) and Death Star for slot 4 (over Sudden Raid), which was re-verified directly in the tracker's Heroic tab.

order.why: First entry in the tracker's Heroic ordering. The Origin skill is the opening unlock and the largest single jump available at the start of 6th job.

order.step: Dark Flare, then Quad Star, then Assassin's Mark mastery cores to level 1
order.why: Entries 2, 3 and 4 in the Heroic ordering, in that sequence. Unlocking a mastery core at level 1 is cheap relative to the damage it adds, so all three main mastery cores are switched on before any is levelled further.
Entry 5, immediately after the three mastery unlocks in the Heroic (fragment-gated) ordering.

order.step: Climb Assassin's Mark and Quad Star together toward level 4-6, with Dark Flare trailing
order.why: Assassin's Mark leads Quad Star slightly in the Heroic ordering, where fragments rather than Sol Erda are the bottleneck: the sheet runs Assassin's Mark 2, Quad Star 2, Assassin's Mark 3-4, Dark Flare 2, Quad Star 3, and so on.

order.step: Throwing Star Barrage boost core to 1, then the class common core (Shadow Walker / Ultimate Dark Sight VI) to 1, then Throw Blasting boost core to 1
order.why: The cheap level-1 unlocks are slotted between mastery levels rather than saved for later - they land at entries 12, 15 and 18 of the Heroic ordering.

order.step: Death Star mastery core from 1 to 4 in one block
order.why: Death Star enters at entry 19, later than the other three masteries, and is then pushed four levels back to back (entries 19-22).

order.step: Dark Lord's Omen boost core to level 1
order.why: Entry 25, another cheap unlock folded into the level 4-6 band.

order.step: Take Quad Star, Assassin's Mark, Dark Flare and Death Star to level 9 before crossing any of them into level 10
order.why: Level 10 is a cost breakpoint on every HEXA node, so the tracker fills all four masteries to 9 first: Assassin's Mark 9, Death Star 9, Quad Star 9 and Dark Flare 9 all land before Assassin's Mark 10. Shurrikane's boost core and Deep Strike (Ascent) take their level-1 unlocks inside this same band.

order.step: Assassin's Mark 10 to 18 first among the level-10-plus pushes, with Life and Death 2-4 and Sol Hecate 2-3 levelled alongside it
order.why: Assassin's Mark is the first core taken past the level 10 breakpoint in the Heroic ordering and runs to 18 before any other core crosses 10. CORRECTION: a previous revision said 'Assassin's Mark 10 to 19'; the sheet interrupts at 18 and only returns for level 19 after Death Star and Quad Star have had their own pushes.

order.step: Death Star 10 to 15, then Quad Star 10 to 14, then Assassin's Mark 19 with Quad Star 15 and Death Star 16, then Dark Flare 10 to 14
order.why: Order of the second-tier pushes after Assassin's Mark clears the breakpoint, read directly off the Heroic tab. CORRECTION: a previous revision compressed this to 'Death Star 10 to 16, then Quad Star 10 to 16, then Dark Flare 10 to 15', which overstates how cleanly the blocks separate.

The tracker places all three HEXA Stat entries together, immediately after Assassin's Mark 19, Quad Star 15 and Dark Flare 14, and before Dark Flare 15 and Quad Star 16. The class doc's prose gives a different rule of thumb (see conflicts): max HEXA Stat 1 and 2 once HEXA Quad Star and HEXA Assassin's Mark are at level 9, because pushing those two to 10 is very expensive.

hexa.orderNote: Every step above was re-read directly from the v271 tracker's Heroic tab in this pass rather than taken on trust. sourceCount is 1 throughout because the tracker and the class doc are one community, not two opinions.

hexaStats.targetLevel: Take each HEXA Stat core to level 20 and stop there, because rerolling is expensive.
hexaStats.placementRule: Recommended shape is core 1 = Attack / main stat / Crit Damage, core 2 = main stat / Crit Damage / Attack, core 3 = Crit Damage / Attack / main stat. The class doc is explicit that this is a template, not a fixed assignment: reorder each roll so the largest value sits on Attack, the next largest on the next priority, and so on. Its own worked example is that a roll of 4-10-6 becomes Crit Damage - Attack - main stat. The doc also says there is no guaranteed flowchart and points at Maple Scouter or another stat calculator for comparing rolls.
hexaStats.spread: HEXA Stat configurations sit roughly half a percent of final damage apart, so there are no genuinely bad rolls. Good rolls are either very high main stat, for a larger absolute stat gain, or very low main stat, for better damage per fragment.
hexaStats.toolNote: Maplescouter's HEXA efficiency output refers only to HEXA Stat core 3; it assumes cores 1 and 2 are already levelled and leaves them out of the ordering.

solJanus.recommendation: For Heroic and early Night Lord grinding, Sol Janus: Dusk at level 1 is enough. Dawn is the better pick for a semi-active farmer or when running Frenzy. Dark Flare triggers Dusk but not Dawn.
solJanus.detail: Dusk hits 9 mobs at level 1, 10 at level 15, 11 at level 30. Dawn gives 1 ring at level 1, 2 at level 10, 3 at level 20. The class doc's author states as a personal preference that they level Sol Janus as their first HEXA skill because Dusk helps farming so much; that is flagged in the doc as opinion, and the Discord's own tracker keeps Sol Janus in a separate column that does not appear in the main Heroic ordering.
solJanus.interaction: It is better for Dark Flare to need more than three hits to kill a mob, so a second Dusk proc is guaranteed even with nothing adjacent to hit with Showdown. Being overgeared for the map therefore reduces Dusk uptime.

solHecate.styx: Styx has a 60-second cooldown even at level 1, so bind it to a 60-second-cooldown skill used near the end of both sequences. Last Resort is the example given.
solHecate.phlegethon: Phlegethon is only used in the main burst, so bind it to a 120-second-cooldown skill used near the end of the sequence. Throwing Star Barrage is the example given.

finalDamageTable.note: Final damage contribution per HEXA skill at levels 1 / 10 / 20 / 30, from KMS data the class doc sourced from maplebot.io in May 2026 and reconfirmed in July 2026. The doc tells readers to take the numbers with a grain of salt. Total from these skills is stated as 112.074%. Row labels here match the doc except that the doc writes 'Marks' for Assassin's Mark and 'Barrage' for Throwing Star Barrage.
finalDamageTable.nameNote: The last row is the job-group common core; see hexa.nodeLayout.classCommonCoreNote. The class doc writes it as 'Ultimate Dark Sight'; the v271 tracker calls the same node 'Shadow Walker'. A wiki-wide search of maplestorywiki.net returns no page for either 'Ultimate Dark Sight' or 'Ultimate Dark Sight VI', so the GMS in-game string is unconfirmed by the wiki.

totalCost.note: Total to take every tracked Night Lord HEXA node to target: Origin and Ascent to 30, the four chosen mastery cores to 30, the four boost cores to 30, Sol Janus and Sol Hecate to 30, the class common core to 30, and three HEXA Stat cores. Both totals were read directly off the tracker's Heroic tab progression block in this pass.

hexa.notes: SOURCING CAVEAT: the HEXA ordering above comes from a single source family. The Night Lord Discord's v271 tracker spreadsheet and the Night Lord class doc are the same community; Grandis Library has no HEXA section at all for this class, and no source outside that Discord publishes a Night Lord HEXA order. Treat the order as the Night Lord Discord's position, not a cross-checked consensus - that is why every entry above is labelled sourceCount 1 and consensus weak even though it was re-verified first-hand. The Heroic ordering is fragment-bottlenecked and the Interactive ordering is Sol Erda-bottlenecked, and they differ materially: Heroic interleaves small level steps across several cores, while Interactive front-loads whole blocks. Use the Heroic tab for GMS Heroic. The class doc also points at Maplescouter to answer 'what next' for a specific character rather than following a static list. Upcoming change: KMS ver. 1.2.417 (July 2026) added a third HEXA skill core with a new Night Lord skill named Shadow Ritual; it had not reached GMS as of this guide's date and will change the ordering when it lands.

hyperStats.notes: The Night Lord class doc deliberately declines to publish a fixed hyper stat order. Its entire hyper stat section reads: hyper stats are largely dependent on your own individual stats and what your character needs; you will always want to maintain 100% critical rate, but the other stats vary with progression; a popular calculator is MathBro's Hyper Stat Optimizer. Recording a static priority list here would misrepresent the source, so priority is null by design, not by omission.
rules: Do not buy critical rate with hyper stat points. The class doc's crit-rate source table marks the Hyper Stat entry 'not recommended since you can get from so many other sources and hyper stat is better used elsewhere', and marks the Legion Outer Grid the same way.
hyperStats.doNotBuyCorrection: 'Attack Speed' was removed from this list. There is no attack speed hyper stat in the game: maplestorywiki's Hyper Stats page enumerates every allocatable stat (STR, DEX, INT, LUK, HP, MP, Demon Fury / Time Force, Critical Rate, Critical Damage, Ignore Defense, Damage, Boss Damage, Normal Damage, Status Resistance, Attack Power & Magic ATT, Experience Obtained, Arcane Force) and attack speed is not among them. The class doc only ever says Night Lord does not need the Attack Speed +1 INNER ABILITY line to reach the cap; a previous revision of this file promoted that inner ability line into a hyper stat that does not exist. See innerAbility.doNotRoll for the claim that is actually supported.

hyperSkills.availabilityNote: The nine passives and three actives were re-read from maplestorywiki's Night Lord skill tables in this pass. Game fact, not opinion.

builds.name: Bossing
builds.why: The only build the class doc publishes, and Grandis Library lists the identical five. Effect values confirmed against maplestorywiki: Frailty Curse - Boss Rush makes the curse apply to bosses at all, Frailty Curse - Enhance adds a further 10% Attack Power and Defense reduction, Quad Star - Reinforce is Damage +20%, Quad Star - Boss Rush is Boss Damage +20%, and Quad Star - Extra Strike is 1 additional attack.

builds.name: Hybrid
builds.why: Trades Frailty Curse - Enhance for Showdown - Enhance to keep some farming value while retaining the boss-facing curse and the full Quad Star package. Grandis Library only; the class doc publishes no hybrid set.

builds.name: Training
builds.why: All three Showdown lines for farming, keeping two Quad Star lines so the character is not useless on a boss. Grandis Library only; the class doc publishes no training set.

hyperSkills.notes: CONSENSUS LABEL CORRECTED DOWN. The bossing build was previously labelled 'strong' on three sources. Grandis Library's credits block attributes its hyper passive build to the Class Doc, so it is a restatement of the same source rather than an independent confirmation, and maplestorywiki carries the skill effects but no build recommendation. That leaves one independent lane, so the honest label is weak. The five passives in each build are an unordered set because none of the sources ranks them - a hyper passive is either taken or not. The three hyper actives are not really a choice: there are exactly three and they are the only actives available.

lines.line: Damage to enemies with Abnormal Status +8%

bossing.why: The class doc states Night Lord's ideal inner ability is Boss Damage, Attack, and Damage to Abnormal. Attack +21 now beats Buff Duration +38% on line 2 because more buff duration sources exist, the current sequence casts faster so Terms and Conditions is used more efficiently, the v263 patch cut Throw Blasting from 68 charms to 46, and HEXA Death Star burns about 20 charms almost immediately. The doc's version history records the switch in two steps: December 2024 (prefer Attack if buff duration is already over 50%, following the DPM meta shift) and September 2025 (stop recommending the buff duration line at all). The abnormal-status line works because Night Lord applies its own debuffs. The doc adds that if you are low on Honor EXP and choosing between them, Damage to Abnormal Status is strictly better than Attack +21.
bossing.labelNote: Three pages state this set and all three were re-read in this pass, but they are not three opinions: Grandis Library credits its inner ability recommendation to the Class Doc, and MapleDoro links out to Grandis and lists the identical three lines under both Bossing and Mobbing, which reads as placeholder content. One independent lane, so weak.

training.why: The class doc publishes exactly these two columns, FARMING 1 and FARMING 2; Grandis states the same thing as 'Meso Obtained / Item Drop Rate +20%' then '+15%'. Which of meso or drop goes on the Legendary line is a farming-goal choice, not a damage one.

alternates.meso: The class doc says a meso line on slot 1 or 2 is fine while grinding and is ultimately personal preference, trading damage for meso.
alternates.dropRate: The class doc calls drop rate an extremely viable line to run, because it affects Oz boxes, pitched boss drops, nodestones and 6th job Sol Erda and fragments.

doNotRoll.why: Night Lord already reaches the attack speed cap (AS0, level/stage 10) without it: 6 from the Claw, 2 from Agile Claws, 1 from Decent Speed Infusion and 1 from a green potion. The class doc's exact wording is 'Night Lord does not need Attack Speed inner ability to reach AS0 (Level/Stage 10)'.
doNotRoll.exception: The class doc does NOT state this as absolute. Under 'Alternate Inner Abilities' it marks attack speed 'Not recommended' but adds that if you cannot roll boss damage or another useful line, or are running out of Honor EXP, the attack speed line lets you save a node slot on Speed Infusion or avoid using a green potion - while still concluding the line is not recommended to keep. Record it as a strong default, not a prohibition.
doNotRoll.labelNote: CITATION CORRECTED. A previous revision cited Grandis Library alongside the class doc and labelled this 'strong'. Grandis's Night Lord page mentions attack speed only in its base-stats table (Stage 8, from the Claw plus Agile Claws) and makes no inner ability recommendation about it, so it does not support the claim. Class doc only.

innerAbility.notes: Rolling all three lines to this shape costs millions of Honor EXP even during a 50% inner ability event; the class doc points at MathBro's Inner Ability Calculator for the estimate and suggests settling for imperfect lines if you have not amassed Honor EXP.

gearingNotes:
CRITICAL RATE. Night Lord has one of the highest base critical rates in the game at 75%: 5% base, 50% from Critical Throw (2nd job) and 20% from Expert Throwing Star Handling (3rd job). Getting to 100% is therefore cheap and should come from Night Lord and Marksman legion member bonuses (up to 5% each), Decent Sharp Eyes (10%), Sayram's Elixir (20%), Lynn's Focus Spirit link (10%), Holy/Rebel/Ocean badges (1% each) and up to 20% from the Legion Artifact. The class doc explicitly advises against buying crit rate with hyper stat points or the legion outer grid, because both are better spent elsewhere. This is the single biggest way Night Lord's gearing differs from a class that has to buy crit.

ATTACK SPEED. Night Lord reaches the cap (stage 10 / AS0) without any attack speed inner ability line: 6 from the Claw, +2 from Agile Claws, +1 from Decent Speed Infusion, +1 from a green potion. There is no attack speed hyper stat to avoid.

IED. Frailty Curse contributes 41% IED against bosses at level 31 with the hyper passive, which is unusually large and means Night Lord's visual IED requirement is lower than most classes'. With 95.47% visual IED plus Frailty Curse, total effective IED is 97.33%, which reaches 90% damage on 380% PDR bosses. Stated requirements: 300% PDR bosses (Lotus, Damien, Lucid, Will, Gloom, Verus Hilla, Darknell, Black Mage) need 94.35% visual, reaching 96.67% cumulative; 380% PDR bosses (Seren, Kalos, Kaling, Limbo, Baldrix) need 95.54% visual, reaching 97.37% cumulative. The class doc rewrote this section in October 2024 to exclude the +20% IED that boost nodes grant, because a lot of Night Lord's damage comes from skill (job) nodes, which grant no IED boost - so do not count skill-sourced IED when planning gear.

BUFF DURATION. Night Lord used to need at least 50% buff duration so Terms and Conditions covered every Throw Blasting charm; that is no longer the binding constraint (see innerAbility). Sources named: 40% legion grid, 25% from a level 250 Mechanic legion block, 10% from level 100 Empathy, 20% from the Legion Artifact, 10% from Sia's Guiding Stars link. As of June 2026 the Night Lord Discord was discussing deliberately staying under 100% buff duration for Culvert.

WSE POTENTIAL (Heroic). Rough guideline is 9/0/0 attack/boss/IED across the nine weapon-secondary-emblem lines as best and 8/1/0 second; the two are close and boss familiars shift the balance. A double or triple prime beats either. On Interactive, assuming 21% or more attack from bonus potentials, the shape given is weapon 2/1/0, secondary 1/2/0, emblem 2/0/1, and it moves with your familiars.

WEAPON SOUL. Raw damage order given: Mu Gong Soul, then Attack +3%, then Boss Damage +7%. Mu Gong must be level 2 for the 20-second duration, its duration is not extended by buff duration from inner ability or legion, it needs charging, the charge is lost on death, and it cannot be used in Culvert.

SECONDARY. Princess No's Charm is called BIS, with Astra as the eventual BIS once strong enough to obtain it.

COOLDOWN HAT. Night Lord does not need one. The Discord's stated positions: a stat hat has the strongest burst; a permanent -2 cooldown hat is roughly equal in full-rotation DPM and adds mini-burst quality of life; -4 or more is slightly weaker but can buy a seventeenth burst in a min-cut run; a -4 hat with a stat line is about equal to a 36% stat line; swapping between a stat hat and a cooldown hat is probably the highest output but needs two finished eternal hats.

THROWING STARS. Attack values matter. Listed by attack: Balanced Fury (30) from Phantom Forest dailies, Flaming Throwing Stars (29, craftable), Crystal Ilbi Throwing Stars (29, Phantom Forest dailies), White Gold Throwing Star (28), Infinite Throwing-Knives (27), Maple-Throwing Stars (21).

RINGS. Night Lord needs Ring of Restraint; the class doc is unambiguous, and the whole burst is built around the RoR window. As of September 2026 the doc notes every class uses RoR and Continuous Ring.

commonMistakes.mistake: Standing too far from the boss during Throwing Star Barrage
commonMistakes.detail: Barrage throws in a fan. At correct range a throw lands 25 attacks: 10 from HEXA Quad Star (5 from you, 5 from Shadow Partner) plus 15 from Barrage (three extra directions of five). Too far out and stars miss entirely.

commonMistakes.mistake: Buying critical rate with hyper stat points or the legion outer grid
commonMistakes.detail: Night Lord starts at 75% crit and can reach 100% from legion members, links, badges, potions and the artifact. The class doc marks both the Hyper Stat and the Legion Outer Grid crit sources 'not recommended'.

commonMistakes.mistake: Rolling the Attack Speed +1 inner ability line
commonMistakes.detail: The class already caps attack speed from Claw base, Agile Claws, Decent Speed Infusion and a green potion, so the line is not recommended to keep - though the class doc allows it as a fallback if you cannot roll boss damage or another useful line. CORRECTED: this entry previously also warned against 'buying attack speed hyper stat'. No attack speed hyper stat exists; maplestorywiki's Hyper Stats page lists all seventeen allocatable stats and attack speed is not one of them.

commonMistakes.mistake: Accidentally entering Last Resort stage 1 instead of stage 2
commonMistakes.detail: With Action Customization on, the down arrow plus the skill key enters stage 1 (+10% final damage, 30 seconds) rather than stage 2 (+24% final damage, 15 seconds if entered immediately). Easy to do while ducking during burst setup.

commonMistakes.mistake: Never triggering Dark Lord's Omen early
commonMistakes.detail: Omen is normally left to explode on its own with the burst, but detonating it early is correct when the boss is about to leave (Lucid disappearing in phase 2, Seren about to dash away), to finish the current phase so Throw Blasting charms carry to the next one, or in Hard Limbo and Hard Baldrix min-clear parties.

commonMistakes.mistake: Being overgeared for the map you farm on
commonMistakes.detail: Sol Janus: Dusk needs mobs to survive long enough to proc. If Dark Flare kills in three hits or fewer, you lose a guaranteed second Dusk proc.

commonMistakes.mistake: Counting boost-node IED when planning gear
commonMistakes.detail: Boost nodes grant +20% Ignore Enemy Defense at level 40, but skill (job) nodes do not, and a lot of Night Lord's damage comes from job-node skills such as Throw Blasting, Shurrikane and Dark Lord's Omen. The class doc rewrote its IED section in October 2024 to leave skill-sourced IED out of the calculation entirely. CORRECTED: a previous revision framed this as Quad Star Boost and Assassin's Mark Boost being special IED sources; the +20% at level 40 is a general boost-node property, not a Night Lord perk.

sources.what: Night Lord Guide, written and maintained by @Lukishi for the Night Lord Discord, succeeding spicedcuttlefish's Night Lord FAQ. Covers V matrix boost/job/common nodes, HEXA structure and HEXA Stat rules, Sol Janus and Sol Hecate binding, hyper passives, inner ability, crit rate, attack speed, IED, buff duration, WSE, weapon soul, cooldown hat, throwing stars and rings. Primary source for almost everything in this file. Re-read in full in this pass; its version history was used to date several recommendations.

Night Lord 6th Tracker [v271], tabs 'v271 VI Tracker (Heroic)' and 'v271 VI Tracker (Interactive)'. Holds the step-by-step HEXA levelling order, per-level Sol Erda and fragment costs, and the 1708 Sol Erda / 47376 fragment totals. Read directly in this pass via CSV export of the Heroic tab, so the order, the totals, the four chosen mastery cores, the four boost cores and the 'ClassCommon' type on the Shadow Walker node are all first-hand. Its default tab still contains Wind Archer rows, corroborating its own header note that it is a template passed from the Wind Archer Discord through Shade, Battle Mage and Angelic Buster to Night Lord - so it shares the class doc's community and is NOT an independent second opinion.
sources.dated: v.271 per tab names; no explicit edit date visible

sources.what: Grandis Library Night Lord page. Boost nodes shown as six numbered nodes with a colour-coded tier, three hyper passive builds, recommended inner ability, link skill, base stats from skills, Dark Sight avoidability chart. Its credits block attributes inner ability, hyper passive build and boost nodes to the Class Doc, so it restates the Lukishi guide rather than confirming it. It has no HEXA section. In this pass the rendered HTML and the site stylesheet were read directly to resolve the node tiers by colour, because a text extraction of the page mislabels them.
sources.dated: GMS Ver. 269 (site-wide stamp; two patches behind v.271)

sources.what: mastermysty's cross-class boost node trio reference. Night Lord entry gives Trio 1 as Showdown / Quad Star / Assassin's Mark and Trio 2 as Sudden Raid / Death Star / Dark Flare. OBSOLETE for trio composition: boost node trios no longer exist, and this page's groupings contradict the current fixed six-node layout. Still useful as an independent lane confirming which six skills are worth building.

Authoritative name and mechanics table, used here as an anti-fabrication check. Re-read via the wiki API in this pass. Confirms: Skill cores Life and Death (Origin) and Deep Strike (Ascent); Mastery core 1 HEXA Quad Star, core 2 HEXA Assassin's Mark, core 3 a choice of HEXA Dark Flare / HEXA Showdown / Darkness Shuriken, core 4 a choice of HEXA Sudden Raid / HEXA Death Star; HEXA Enhancement cores Throw Blasting Boost, Throwing Star Barrage Boost, Shurrikane Boost, Dark Lord's Omen Boost; Shared HEXA Skills Sol Janus and Sol Hecate; the nine hyper passives with their exact effect values and the three hyper actives. Carries no priority judgement. Returns 403 to plain fetching; readable via the MediaWiki API with a browser user agent.

Used in this pass to establish that no attack speed hyper stat exists.

Current V Matrix mechanics. Used in this pass to establish that trios no longer exist and that boost-node IED is not Night Lord-specific.

Shadow Walker, the 5th job skill shared by Night Lord, Shadower and Blade Master. Max level 30, 20-second stealth not cancelled by attacks or skills. Used to reconcile the class doc's 'Ultimate Dark Sight' with the tracker's 'Shadow Walker'.

positionA.heldBy: Lukishi's Night Lord guide, restated by Grandis Library and MapleDoro
positionA.reasoning: More buff duration sources exist now, the faster sequence makes Terms and Conditions more efficient, v263 cut Throw Blasting from 68 to 46 charms, and HEXA Death Star consumes roughly 20 charms almost immediately.

positionB.claim: Boss Damage +20%, Buff Duration +38%, Damage to Abnormal Status +8%
positionB.heldBy: A video guide by Hooning, presented in the class doc itself as the devil's advocate case
positionB.reasoning: Not recorded in the class doc beyond the recommendation itself; the historical rationale was keeping Terms and Conditions up long enough to spend every Throw Blasting charm.

conflicts.status: Contested. The Attack +21 position is current and better argued, and the class doc's version history dates the switch to December 2024 and September 2025. The dissent is recorded in the class doc itself rather than dismissed. The video was not located or read directly in this pass, so position B is known only through the class doc's summary of it.

conflicts.topic: When to invest in HEXA Stat cores 1 and 2

positionA.claim: Max HEXA Stat 1 and 2 once HEXA Quad Star and HEXA Assassin's Mark are at level 9, because pushing those two past the level 10 breakpoint is very expensive.

positionB.claim: The three HEXA Stat entries sit later, after Assassin's Mark reaches 19, Quad Star 15 and Dark Flare 14.
positionB.heldBy: The Night Lord Discord's v271 Heroic tracker ordering

conflicts.status: Unresolved inconsistency within one source family, and position B was confirmed exactly in this pass by reading the Heroic tab: Hexa Stat levels 1, 2 and 3 fall immediately after Assassin's Mark 19, Quad Star 15 and Dark Flare 14. The doc itself concedes it is hard to say exactly when to level HEXA Stat 1 and 2 and calls its own answer a general recommendation.

conflicts.topic: Sol Janus as a first HEXA investment

positionA.claim: Level Sol Janus first, because Dusk mode transforms farming.
positionA.heldBy: Lukishi, stated explicitly as personal preference ('I personally like to level Sol Janus as my first hexa skill')

positionB.claim: Sol Janus is tracked in its own separate column and does not appear in the main Heroic ordering, which opens with Life and Death, the three mastery unlocks and Sol Hecate.

conflicts.status: Not really contested on the facts - one is a farming quality-of-life preference and the other is a damage ordering - but a planner should not present 'Sol Janus first' as the consensus build order. Position B re-confirmed in this pass: Sol Janus occupies its own column in the Heroic tab, separate from the main priority column.

sourcingCaveats.detail: Only two independent lanes carry judgement for Night Lord: (1) the Night Lord Discord lineage - Lukishi's guide, the v271 tracker spreadsheet and Grandis Library's page, which are one family because Grandis credits the Class Doc and the tracker comes from the same Discord; and (2) mastermysty's node guide, which is independent but dated 2024 and whose trio groupings are now obsolete. maplestorywiki.net and Orange Mushroom are genuinely independent but carry game facts and patch notes only, no priorities. MapleDoro's Night Lord page is largely placeholder and links to Grandis. Reddit was not reachable in this pass and the Night Lord Discord was not read. CONSEQUENCE: no claim in this file reaches the three-independent-source bar, so nothing is labelled 'strong'. A previous revision labelled eight endgame claims 'strong' by counting Grandis Library and the tracker as separate voices; they are not.

contest.method: An independent agent re-searched every claim in this file without seeing the researcher's reasoning, and was instructed to refute rather than confirm. A resolution pass on 2026-09-12 then reopened each cited page and settled the endgame defects.

resolved.defect: THERE IS NO ATTACK SPEED HYPER STAT. hyperStats.doNotBuy listed 'Attack Speed', hyperStats.notes said the attack speed hyper stat is unnecessary, and commonMistakes warned against buying it.
resolved.action: Re-read maplestorywiki's Hyper Stats page via the MediaWiki API. It enumerates seventeen allocatable stats and attack speed is not among them. Re-read the class doc: it says only 'Night Lord does not need Attack Speed inner ability to reach AS0 (Level/Stage 10)' and discusses attack speed solely as an inner ability line. Removed 'Attack Speed' from hyperStats.doNotBuy, rewrote hyperStats.notes around what the doc actually says, added hyperStats.doNotBuyCorrection recording the error, and rewrote the commonMistakes entry to be about the inner ability line only.

resolved.defect: CONFLICT #4 ATTRIBUTED A POSITION TO GRANDIS LIBRARY THAT GRANDIS DOES NOT HOLD - the file claimed Grandis files Showdown/Dark Flare/Death Star/Sudden Raid as Secondary while the class doc calls them Essential.
resolved.action: Fetched the Grandis page's raw HTML and its stylesheet. The tier colours resolve as PRIMARY #2e94b6 and SECONDARY #cc6a2a; Night Lord Nodes 1, 2, 3 and 4 all carry #2E94B6 (Primary) and Nodes 5 and 6 carry #6C757D (Other). No node on the page is Secondary. The class doc's own table labels the same six nodes Essential, Essential, Essential, Essential, Skip, Skip. The two sources agree exactly and the conflict was invented, so the entire conflict entry was deleted. A markdown text extraction of the Grandis page does report a Secondary tier; it is wrong, and the raw HTML plus stylesheet is the authority.

resolved.defect: 'Ultimate Dark Sight' in hexa.finalDamageTable has zero hits on maplestorywiki, and the file also called what looks like the same node 'Shadow Walker' in hexa.nodeLayout.classCommonCore without reconciling them.
resolved.action: The naming inconsistency was real and is now fixed; the 'does not exist' half is not. Ultimate Dark Sight VI is the Explorer Thief job-group common HEXA core added in KMS ver. 1.2.414 (April 2026), reported by Orange Mushroom, whose description - attack and use skills in Dark Sight without it being cancelled - matches the 5th job thief skill Shadow Walker on maplestorywiki. The v271 tracker tracks this node under the name 'Shadow Walker' with type 'ClassCommon' and 31 levels; the class doc lists it as 'Ultimate Dark Sight' under Common Skills. Both names now appear together with an explanation in classCommonCoreNote and finalDamageTable.nameNote, and the residual uncertainty - that maplestorywiki has no page for the core, so its GMS string is unconfirmed - is recorded in sourcingCaveats.notReached rather than hidden.

resolved.defect: NEW, found during resolution: vMatrix.trios asserted two boost node trios and cited the class doc, Grandis Library and mastermysty for both.
resolved.action: Boost node trios no longer exist. maplestorywiki's V Matrix page states every player receives a fixed set of six boost nodes, each enhancing one to four skills, and the class doc's version history for 11 July 2026 says it simplified its V Matrix section 'now that trios are gone'. Only mastermysty publishes Night Lord trios, its data is dated 2024-05-14, and its groupings contradict the class doc and Grandis, which both pair Showdown with Dark Flare and Death Star with Sudden Raid. Citing those two sources in support of the trios was a citation inversion. vMatrix.trios is now an empty array with vMatrix.triosNote explaining why.

resolved.defect: NEW, found during resolution: vMatrix.priority shipped six individually ranked boost nodes, ranking Showdown above Dark Flare and Death Star above Sudden Raid.
resolved.action: No source ranks within those pairs, and the pairs cannot be ranked - Showdown and Dark Flare share one boost node, as do Death Star and Sudden Raid. The array now holds six node entries matching the numbering both sources use, each with a skills list and a 'skillsOrdered' flag that is false for the two paired nodes, plus a priorityNote telling downstream code not to read those pairs as a ranking.

resolved.defect: NEW, found during resolution: vMatrix.priority claimed the Quad Star and Assassin's Mark boost nodes are two of the few reliable +20% Ignore Enemy Defense sources for Night Lord.
resolved.action: maplestorywiki's V Matrix page states boost nodes generally grant +20% Ignored Enemy Defense at level 40 - it is not specific to those two nodes. The class doc's own version history records rewriting its IED section in October 2024 to EXCLUDE boost-node IED from gear planning. The claim inverted its source's advice. Removed from both node entries and replaced with an explicit correction in vMatrix.notes and the matching commonMistakes entry.

resolved.defect: NEW, found during resolution: innerAbility.doNotRoll cited Grandis Library and was labelled consensus 'strong'.
resolved.action: Grandis's Night Lord page mentions attack speed only in its base-stats table (Stage 8, from the Claw plus Agile Claws) and makes no inner ability recommendation about it. Citation removed, sourceCount set to 1, consensus set to weak, and the class doc's own conditional exception - the line is acceptable as a fallback if you cannot roll boss damage or are short on Honor EXP - added, because the previous flat prohibition overstated the source.

resolved.defect: NEW, found during resolution: eight endgame claims were labelled consensus 'strong' on three sources that included Grandis Library and the v271 tracker alongside the class doc.
resolved.action: Grandis credits the Class Doc for boost nodes, hyper passives and inner ability, and the tracker comes from the same Discord; mirrors of one document count once. Every endgame claim was relabelled with an honest sourceCount and consensus. Nothing in the file is now labelled 'strong'. The vMatrix node tiering is the best-sourced claim at two independent lanes and is labelled moderate.

resolved.defect: NEW, found during resolution: two hexa.order steps described the tracker's level-10-plus pushes more cleanly than the sheet does.
resolved.action: The Heroic tab was exported and read row by row. Assassin's Mark runs 10 to 18, not 10 to 19, before any other core crosses the breakpoint; the second-tier pushes interleave as Death Star 10-15, Quad Star 10-14, then Assassin's Mark 19, Quad Star 15, Death Star 16, then Dark Flare 10-14. Both steps rewritten to match, with the prior wording noted. Every other step in hexa.order, the 1708 / 47376 totals, the four chosen mastery cores and the four boost cores were confirmed unchanged against the same export.
